news_drafts.headline: Denbighshire rates its financial sustainability risk "critical" at C1; Audit Wales faults Section 114 guidance
news_drafts.lead:
Denbighshire County Council's corporate risk register gives financial sustainability a residual score of C1, which it classes as "critical". The inherent score, before the council's controls are counted, is A1. The register states that the risk is outside the council's appetite and that both scores are likely to remain high.

The register describes the risk as demand and resource pressures exceeding the council's sustainable capacity to deliver statutory services. Among its listed impacts are an inability to agree and set a balanced budget and a risk of a Section 114 notice, the formal declaration by a council's chief finance officer that it cannot balance its budget.

The Governance and Audit Committee also considered an Audit Wales report on local government funding. It found that the Welsh Government "had not clearly set out the support available in the event of a Section 114 report". The report also found that the settlement methodology had not been fully and independently reviewed since 2002 and that restricted grants can be confirmed late. It made five recommendations to the Welsh Government, covering the settlement process, restricted grants, medium-term funding information, the costs of new responsibilities and support for councils in significant financial difficulty. The committee agreed to refer the report to the Scrutiny Chairs and Vice-Chairs Group.

news_drafts.headline: Denbighshire's 2027/28 budget gap would be £8m after a 5.3% council tax rise, down from May forecast
news_drafts.lead:
Denbighshire County Council's budget gap for 2027/28 would be £8m after a mid-range council tax rise of 5.3%, according to its medium term financial strategy and plan. The rise would yield an additional £4.7m, which the paper says addresses roughly a third of the funding gap. The paper, before the Performance Scrutiny Committee on 12 November, calls the remaining £8m "substantial" and says it has come down from the last forecast in May.

Over the three years from 2027/28 to 2029/30, the forecast gap ranges from a low of £19m to a high of £36m, with a mid-range projection of £27m. The paper says the figures are uncertain and that further work is needed to refine them. The plan's council tax assumptions for 2027/28 range from 4% to 7%.

The paper also sets out the council tax rises that would bridge the total gap under its low, medium and high scenarios: 11%, 15% and 20%. It describes these as theoretical and as assuming no savings are achieved. It says a 15% rise would in theory balance the budget without reductions, and that no decisions have been made.

news_drafts.headline: Denbighshire forecasts £5.2m overspend for 2026/27, with schools £5.4m over budget
news_drafts.lead:
Denbighshire County Council's Cabinet was told on 20 October that the council expects to end 2026/27 having spent £314.1m against a budget of £308.9m, a forecast overspend of £5.2m, or 1.7%. A forecast overspend is where a council expects to finish the year having spent more than it budgeted.

The schools budget, including the part of school funding the council does not pass directly to schools, is forecast at £103.9m against a budget of £98.5m. That is £5.4m, or 5.4%, over. It is the largest variance of any service in the budget summary, and it is larger than the overspend for the council as a whole.

The council's savings programme, the cuts and efficiencies it has committed to in order to balance its budget, set a target of £3.17m for 2026/27. The savings tracker shows £1.82m achieved, or 57.4%. A further £701k, 22.1%, is in progress. Proposals worth £648k, 20.4%, are marked "not achieved", and £738k of the target remains undelivered. The papers set out the figures but, in the extracts available, do not say how the council plans to close the gap.

findings.paper_title: Denbighshire County Council - Audit of Accounts report 2023-24 App 3
findings.headline: The auditor concludes that the going concern basis of accounting is appropriate and has identified no material uncertainties about the council's ability to continue.
findings.detail: This conclusion is made in the proposed audit report alongside the intended qualified opinion on the revaluation reserve and capital adjustment account. The paper states the going concern conclusion separately from that qualification.
findings.matters: A going concern conclusion without material uncertainty is the audit finding a lender is most likely to rely on, and it sits alongside the qualification in the same report.
findings.quote: In auditing the financial statements, I have concluded that the use of the going concern basis of accounting in the preparation of the financial statements is appropriate.

findings.paper_title: Denbighshire County Council - Audit of Accounts report 2023-24 App 3
findings.headline: The auditor has made seven recommendations, three of which were brought forward from the 2022-23 audit.
findings.detail: The recommendations cover capital accounting and valuation, reconciliation of populations, related parties, asset valuation approach, Section 106 agreements, leases and the quality of draft statements. Priority is high for six of the seven, with the Section 106 recommendation rated medium.
findings.matters: Recommendations carried over from one year to the next are a measure of how many audit issues remain open, which finance directors at peer councils can use for comparison.
findings.figures: Seven recommendations, of which three were brought forward from 2022-23.
findings.quote: We include seven recommendations as a result of our work, which includes three recommendations brought forward from our 2022-23 audit of accounts report.

findings.paper_title: Denbighshire County Council - Audit of Accounts report 2023-24 App 3
findings.headline: Two elected members failed to declare interests in two organisations, and transactions with both organisations needed to be added to the related party disclosures in Note 32.
findings.detail: Recommendation 3 describes the same issue as one elected member failing to declare a directorship in two organisations, so the paper gives different counts in different places. The council's management response says declarations for 2024-25 and 2025-26 have already been completed.
findings.matters: Completeness of member declarations is a control that finance directors and lenders look at when assessing governance, and the paper shows it was found incomplete.
findings.figures: Two elected members; two organisations; one elected member in the Appendix 5 version.
findings.quote: Two elected members had failed to declare their interests in two separate organisations.

findings.paper_title: Denbighshire County Council - Audit of Accounts report 2023-24 App 3
findings.headline: The council accepts that its draft financial statements for 2022-23 and 2023-24 do not meet the required standards, and a group is to be set up by the end of the calendar year to address the issues.
findings.detail: The management response describes a group of key officers from different disciplines to develop an action plan, with progress reported to the Head of Finance and Audit, CET and GAC. The 2024-25 accounts are the first to be prepared on the new finance system.
findings.matters: Acceptance of poor draft quality, and a new finance system in the first year of IFRS 16, are the reasons finance directors at other councils would give for their own accounts timetables.
findings.figures: Group to be set up by the end of the calendar year; new financial system from 1 April 2024.
findings.quote: The Council accepts that the quality of the draft financial statements for 2022-23 and 2023-24 does not meet the required standards.

findings.paper_title: Denbighshire County Council - Audit of Accounts report 2023-24 App 3
findings.headline: The auditor reports that the residual risk of material misstatement in asset valuations is low, after corrections to the financial statements.
findings.detail: Testing found errors in valuation inputs and missing source data for agricultural land, and the auditor says corrections were made in the statements. The paper says the residual risk across the population is low.
findings.matters: Valuation method and source data are the basis for the asset values lenders and finance directors use, and this paper shows both the errors found and the corrections made.
findings.quote: Our work has confirmed that the residual risk of material misstatement across the population is low.

daily_post.headline: Fixed penalty notices for school attendance do not generate a high level of income for the Education Service.
daily_post.lead: A council may assume enforcement income offsets service costs; this paper records that it does not, which matters to finance officers assessing similar income streams.
